rationale: Lycopolitan ⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ = Coptic ⲁⲍⲙⲉ/ⲱⲱⲙⲉ 'well, cistern, pit' (Crum 480a, 525a). In this kephalaion designates the three cosmic source-points / root-wells spanning the Deep to the Height. Each is described as the ⲧⲛⲟⲩⲛⲉ 'root' of a cosmic stratum. The chapter title 'Concerning the Wells' (kephalaion 48) introduces them as foundational cosmographic features.

ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ already in glossary as verbal 'to be king/reign'; here functions as a substantival noun 'king' with demonstrative ⲡⲓ-. Confirmed by parallel ⲡⲓⲣⲡⲟ ⲉⲧϣⲏϣ ⲟⲩⲃⲉ ⲡϣⲓ ⲛⲧⲉϩⲙⲛⲧⲣⲡⲟ (line 6) where ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ contrasts with ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲣ̄ⲡⲟ 'kingship.'

Tentative; possibly Lyc. reflex of ⲇⲟⲕⲡⲉ/ⲇⲱⲕⲡⲣ̄ 'be small, decreased' (Crum 511a). Context: paired antithetically with ⲣ̄ⲍⲟⲩⲟ 'multiply' to describe wealth's increase-and-decrease cycle through the way-leaders. Confidence low — flag for parallels.

Compound: ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ⲕⲓⲙ ('move, set in motion'). Standard agent-noun formation paralleling ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' The way-leaders 'are the movers of the entire creation' — active causal agents driving the cosmos.

Greek loanword πτωματικόν from πτῶμα 'fall, corpse.' Paired distinctly with σωματικόν as the second characterization of the lower worlds — they are both 'embodied' and 'cadaverous/fallen.' Standard Manichaean correspondence: lower bodies are fallen carcasses.

Lyc variant of ⲁⲡⲧⲭⲓⲥⲉ 'to the Height' (cf. ⲡⲧⲭⲓⲥⲉ/ⲡⲭⲥⲉ in glossary). The vowel-dilation ⲁⲡⲧⲉⲥⲭⲓⲥⲉ may be scribal. Forms the cosmic vertical axis pair with ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲛ 'the Deep' — the three Wells span this axis.

Tentative parsing as ⲣ̄- ('do/make') + ⲟⲩⲁⲣⲡⲧ qualitative of ⲟⲩⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'send, dispatch' (or alternatively ⲣⲱⲡⲧ̄ 'cast off'). Used of the upper realms sent/cast down to be bound in the lower earths. Low confidence.
Lyc. perfect of ⲛⲟⲩⲝⲉ/ⲛⲟⲩϫ 'throw, cast' with 3pl object suffix. The cosmogonic action of casting the stripped upper realms down to the lower lands.
